 JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed the claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against the respondents for seeking compensation on account of death of one, Sri.Honne Gowda S/o late Made Gowda, in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioner is as under:
That on 31.12.2023 at about 03.30 p.m, on Channapatna - Sathanuru Road, near Kabbalu (v), (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.2945/2024 Sathanur (h), Kanakapura tq,
Ramanagara Dist, the said Honne Gowda was a pedestrian at the road side.

At that time, one Motor Cycle bearing No. JH-05-DF-0685 came from behind i.e., from Channapatna side, in a rash and negligent manner, with excessive speed and dashed against said Honne Gowda and caused the accident.
Due to which the said Honne Gowda fell down on the road and sustained grievous fatal injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Government hospital, Sathanuru and thereafter he was shifted to Spandana hospital, Mandya and later he was shifted to Basavanagudi Medical Centre for further treatment.
But said Honne Gowda died on 09.01.2024.

Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 54 years and was doing agriculture work and milk vendor work and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners have lost love and affection,
social, moral and economical support and they are depending on the earnings of the deceased.
The petitioner No.1 is the daughter and petitioner No.2 is adopted son of the deceased.

Since the deceased Honnegowda's wife and son passed away at earlier,
he adopted the petitioner No.2 as his (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.2945/2024 caretaker.
The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent riding of rider of offending Motor Cycle and in this regard the Sathanuru Police have registered a case against driver of the offending Motor Cycle.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said offending vehicle,
are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- to the petitioners together with cost and interest.
03. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels and have filed objections.

04. The respondent No.1 is his objections has denied the entire case of the petitioners and further denied alleged accident, negligence of the rider of offending Motor Cycle, age, avocation and income of deceased, nature of the injuries sustained by the deceased, treatment taken by the deceased,
dependency of the petitioners with the deceased and expenses incurred by the petitioners and admitted that he is the owner of the offending Motor Cycle and the same is insured with respondent Vidyashree H vs Arpan Jash on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40020734/
2 No.2 and the insurance is active as on the date of accident and the rider of the offending Motor Cycle had valid driving licence at the time of accident and the compensation (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.2945/2024 claimed is highly exorbitant and contended that the deceased Honnegowda appeared intoxicated and uncertain about crossing the road, exhibiting erratic movements.
This respondent has already paid a considerable amount and the fact that deceased was drunk and deliberately jumped before this respondent's Motor Cycle is of significance in this case.

If the court comes to the conclusion that the petitioners are entitled for the compensation, then the respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation and hence prays for dismiss the petition against respondent No.2 with cost.
05.

The respondent No.2 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioners and further denied issuance of insurance policy in the name of Arpan Jash in respect of vehicle bearing No.
JH-05-DF-0685, alleged accident, involvement of offending Motor Cycle in the accident, negligence of the rider of offending Motor Cycle, age, avocation and income of deceased, nature of the injuries sustained by the deceased, treatment taken by the deceased and expenses incurred by the petitioners and denies existence of policy in the name of Arpan Jash in respect of vehicle bearing No.JH-05-DF-0685 and (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.2945/2024 contended that rider of the Motor Cycle is not having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and hence there is violation of breach of the policy conditions.

The compensation claimed is excessive, exorbitant and hence, pray to dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.2.
06.

Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following Issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: -
ISSUES
01. Whether petitioners prove that they are the LRs/dependents of deceased Sri.late Honnegowda S/o late Madegowda?

02. Whether petitioners prove that deceased Sri.late Honnegowda S/o late Madegowda, was died in RTA arising out of the accident alleged to have been taken place on 31.12.2023 at about 3.30 p.m, on Channapatna-Satanur Road, near Kabbalu Village, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District, due to rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing registration No.JH-05-DF-0685 by its rider as alleged in the petition?
03. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
04 . What order or award?
(SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.2945/2024 Vidyashree H vs Arpan Jash on 1 April, 2026

08. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.2 got examined Superintendent, its Legal Manager as RW.1 and 2 and respondent No.1 got examined himself as RW.3 and through them got marked 11 documents as Ex.R.1 to 11 and closed their side evidence.
09. Heard both sides.

The counsel for the petitioners has relied upon the following citations:-

My findings on the aforesaid Issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 In the Affirmative  (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.2945/2024  Issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4

As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS 11. Issue No.1:- Petitioner No.1 in her affidavit stated that she is the daughter and petitioner No.2 is the adopted son of the deceased Honne Gowda.

To prove the said fact, she has produced notarized copy of Aadhaar cards of herself, petitioner No.2 and deceased and Ration card, Death certificates of Doddathayamma and Madesha,
SSLC marks card and Marriage certificate of petitioner No.1 as per Ex.P.11 to 16, 19 and 20, which shows that petitioner No.1 is the daughter and petitioner No.2 is the adopted son of the deceased.

In her cross-examination she has that she has provided documents to show that she is the daughter of the deceased Honnegouda and admits that her name is not on the ration card of Ex.P.14 and father's name of the petitioner No.2 Mahesh is Lingegowda and denied to the suggestion that neither she nor her younger brother have provided documents to show that they are the children of Vidyashree H vs Arpan Jash on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40020734/
4 Honnegowda and admits that deceased Honnegowda had a wife by name (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.2945/2024 Dodda Tayamma and a son by name Madesh and they died and denied to the suggestion that Honnegowda had no heirs after both are died.
But as per the recent Judgment of our Hon'ble High Court even the major sons and married daughters are entitled to claim compensation for the death of their parents on all heads.
There is no serious dispute regarding relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
Hence, this tribunal is of the opinion that petitioners No.1 and 2 are the legal representatives and dependents on the income of the deceased.
Hence, I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

12. Issue No.2:- The petitioners in order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 herself examined as PW.1 and in her chief-examination evidence she has reiterated the petition averments therein.
Though she has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioners.
On perusal of the documents, Ex.P.1 is FIR registered at Sathanoor Police against rider of the offending Motor Cycle.

Ex.P.2 and 3 are the Complaints shows due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of offending Motor Cycle the accident occurred and deceased (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.2945/2024 sustained injuries and later died during the course of treatment.
Ex.P.4 is Requisition given by the Police.

Ex.P.5 and 6 are the Spot Mahazar and Sketch showing the place of accident on Channapatna- Satanur Road, near Durgada Kabbalamma Party Hall and Kumar Party Hall, Kabbalu, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District,
which is not disputed.
Ex.P.7 is IMV report which discloses involvement of offending Motor Cycle in the accident and damages caused to its front side.
Ex.P.8 is Inquest report of deceased Honnegowda.
Ex.P.9 is PM report of deceased Honnegowda shows the cause of death is due to coma as a result of head injury sustained.

Ex.P.10 is Charge sheet shows after completion of investigation the Investigation Officer has filed Charge sheet against rider/respondent No.1 of offending Motor Cycle, for the offences punishable U/s 279, 304(A) of IPC.

The oral and documentary evidence adduced by the petitioners clearly goes to show that the accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the rider of offending Motor Cycle and deceased sustained injuries and later died.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the affirmative.

(SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.2945/2024 13. Issue No.3:- This Issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased Honnegowda, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

The PW.1/petitioner No.1 has stated that prior to accident deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 54 years and was doing agriculture work and milk vendor work and earning Rs.30,000/-
p.m.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners are put to great financial loss, loss of love and affection and mental agony.
14. It is the duty of the petitioner to prove age of the deceased.

The petitioners have not produced any birth certificate, school records, SSLC marks card or even Aadhaar card of the deceased to show Vidyashree H vs Arpan Jash on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40020734/
5 his exact date of birth.
However, they have produced Ex.P.13 Aadhaar card of deceased.

Even though said document is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of other evidence, said document can be relied upon and according to which the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 01.01.1969.
The alleged accident occurred on 31.12.2023 and hence it appears that as on the date of accident the age of the deceased is 54 years.

Therefore,
(SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.2945/2024 this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 54 years and as per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 51 to 55 years is "11".
15.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So far as avocation and income of deceased is concerned, the petitioners have not placed any materials before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2023 to be taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the deceased is at Rs.16,000/- and it is multiplied by 12.
16.
In the case on hand, undoubtedly the petitioner No.1 is the daughter and petitioner No.2 is the adopted son of the deceased and they are the dependents on the earnings of the deceased.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.2945/2024 Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.2945/2024 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since deceased was aged 54 years at the time of accident and he comes in the age group of 50 to 60 years and was self employee, 10% income should be added to the monthly income towards future prospects which would be result in the income to be (16,000 + 1,600) = Rs.17,600/-.

Therefore,
considering the materials available on record, this tribunal is of the opinion that since there are two dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/3rd of the income towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (Rs.17,600 - Rs.5,867) = Rs.11,733/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.11,733/-.
As the deceased was aged about 54 years, the multiplier of 11 would have to be applied.
Consequently the claimants would be entitled for a sum of (Rs.11,733 x 12 x 11) Rs.15,48,756/- is awarded towards loss of dependency.
17. Medical expenses:- The petitioners have produced entire Medical bills and Prescriptions as per Ex.P.17 and 18 for Rs.4,76,018/-.
To disprove the Medical bills, the respondent No.2 has not produced (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.2945/2024 any documents nor any evidence.
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for Rs.4,76,018/- under this head.

18. In view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & Others case, in respect to loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years.

10% is enhanced for period of every 3 years.

6 19.
The claimants No.1 and 2 are the daughter and son of the deceased.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in Magma General Insurance Company Ltd.,
V/s Nanu Ram alias Churu Ram reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, the petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of parental consortium and petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses and transportation of dead body.

Regarding liability:- To disprove the case of the petitioners, the respondent No.2 got examined Superintendent at Community Health Center hospital, Sathanur, as RW.1 and he has produced Authorization letter and MLC extract as per Ex.R.1 and 2, wherein it (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.2945/2024 is mentioned that "Alleged H/O RTA, said to have got hit by two-wheeler while walking in the path on 31.12.2023 around 02.40 p.m, near Kabbalu".

Further, got examined its Legal Manager as RW.2 and in her chief-examination evidence she has reiterated the objections averments therein and in her cross-examination she admits that she has deposed based on the Police documents and investigation report and as per the Police documents when the deceased was walking on the left side of the road the Motor Cycle hit him from behind, but as per their investigation report when the deceased was crossing the road the accident was occurred and they did not question the final report because they are not party members and she has produced Authorization letter and Policy as per Ex.R.1 and 2 which shows that the insurance policy to the offending Motor Cycle is valid and is in force as on the date of accident.

Further, the respondent No.1 got examined himself as RW.3 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the objections averments therein and in his cross-examination he stated that on the day of the accident, he was coming from Mandya to Bengaluru and it is a State highway.
He saw the (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.2945/2024 deceased crossing the road from a distance of 100 meters.
There are no pedestrian crossing marks there and there are no signals there.

The deceased crossed Vidyashree H vs Arpan Jash on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40020734/
7 the road and stood in the middle.
The deceased did not see him.
Suddenly, he turned back and came back to the same road when the accident occurred.
The deceased did not notice the Motor Cycle coming.
The accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased.
He was appearing in JMFC court.

He has paid Rs.1,50,000/- to Siddharaju at the accident site twice through UPI and twice through online and denied to the suggestion that he has not paid any money to the applicant, but to a third party and admits that the driving license and insurance policy were valid at the time of the accident and he has produced Insurance policy, Driving licence of himself, Prescriptions, Medical bills, Online transaction details, Aadhaar card of himself and Certificate U/s 65 B of Evidence Act as per Ex.R.5 to 11 which shows that the insurance policy to the offending Motor Cycle is valid and is in force as on the date of accident and respondent No.1 had valid driving licence and in some of the Medical bills the patient name is mentioned as (SCCH-3) 18 M.V.C.No.2945/2024 Shreevani, hence the said Medical bills is not considered.

On perusal of oral and documentary evidence adduced by the respondents, though it is stated that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased himself in walking or crossing the road,
but in Charge sheet at Ex.P.10 it is stated that the rider of Motor Cycle came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased and caused the accident.

21. The RW.3 deposed that he has paid Rs.1,50,000/- to Siddharaju, the complainant, at the accident site twice through UPI and twice through online and it is evident from Ex.R.9 Online transaction details.

Accordingly I hold that, after deducting the said amount, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.19,91,074/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
On the date of accident the policy was in force.
Hence, respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay above said compensation amount.

(SCCH-3) 19 M.V.C.No.2945/2024 Respondent No.2 Insurance Company is directed to deposit above said compensation amount within two months from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, Issue No.3 is answered partly in the affirmative.
22. Issue No.4:-

In view of reasons assigned to Issues No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:- -
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.19,91,074/- (Rupees Nineteen lakhs ninety one thousand and seventy four only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

The petitioner No.1 being the daughter and petitioner No.2 being the son of the deceased were apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 70-30, in the award amount together with interest.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, the petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled to get release 70% each of the award through E-payment directly to their account by obtaining the bank account details on proper identification without any further proceedings and remaining 30% each shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
The petitioners are at liberty to draw periodical interest.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

The petitioners have filed the claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against the respondents for seeking compensation on account of death of one, Sri.Honne Gowda S/o late Made Gowda, in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent riding of rider of offending Motor Cycle and in this regard the Sathanuru Police have registered a case against driver of the offending Motor Cycle.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said offending vehicle,

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Hence, this tribunal is of the opinion that petitioners No.1 and 2 are the legal representatives and dependents on the income of the deceased.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners are put to great financial loss, loss of love and affection and mental agony.
14. It is the duty of the petitioner to prove age of the deceased.
Even though said document is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of other evidence, said document can be relied upon and according to which the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 01.01.1969.
The alleged accident occurred on 31.12.2023 and hence it appears that as on the date of accident the age of the deceased is 54 years.
Therefore,
(SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.2945/2024 this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 54 years and as per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 51 to 55 years is "11".
15.
In the case on hand, undoubtedly the petitioner No.1 is the daughter and petitioner No.2 is the adopted son of the deceased and they are the dependents on the earnings of the deceased.
In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.2945/2024 Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.
Therefore,
considering the materials available on record, this tribunal is of the opinion that since there are two dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/3rd of the income towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (Rs.17,600 - Rs.5,867) = Rs.11,733/-.
18. In view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & Others case, in respect to loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years.
Accordingly, in the head of loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses,
10% is enhanced for period of every 3 years.
The claimants No.1 and 2 are the daughter and son of the deceased.
In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in Magma General Insurance Company Ltd.,
V/s Nanu Ram alias Churu Ram reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, the petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of parental consortium and petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses and transportation of dead body.

22. Issue No.4:-
In view of reasons assigned to Issues No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:- -
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.19,91,074/- (Rupees Nineteen lakhs ninety one thousand and seventy four only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.
The petitioner No.1 being the daughter and petitioner No.2 being the son of the deceased were apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 70-30, in the award amount together with interest.
On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, the petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled to get release 70% each of the award through E-payment directly to their account by obtaining the bank account details on proper identification without any further proceedings and remaining 30% each shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
The petitioners are at liberty to draw periodical interest.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
